summary: Crawled www.regione.veneto.it by parsing real hrefs at each hop and found a genuine phytosanitary bulletin archive. Path (all links extracted from fetched HTML, none guessed): homepage -> /web/guest/agricoltura -> /web/fitosanitario -> /web/fitosanitario/bollettini-fitosanitari (the archive index, reached at hop 3) -> year pages (hop 4) -> per-crop leaf pages (hop 5). The archive index links exactly three year pages: 2026, 2025, 2024, and its own body text says the previous years available are 2025 and 2024. Index last-updated text: "30 agosto 2026". The archive is NOT uniform across years, which matters for any preservation pass. YEAR 2026 page: 106 unique document links, all PDFs on www.regione.veneto.it/documents/... Classified by filename with zero unclassified: vite 20, olivo 29, frutticolo 25, orticolo 22, erbacee 2, plus 8 "calendario recapiti" files that are office-hours schedules, NOT bulletins. The 20 vite items state dates 09/04/2026 through 27/08/2026 (N.01-N.20). YEAR 2025 page: 133 unique document links; the 20 vite items are NOT on the portal - they are Nextcloud share links on a second host, sharing.regione.veneto.it/index.php/s/<token>, which serve the PDF only when /download is appended (the bare share URL returns a 27,609-byte HTML viewer). Dates stated: 09/04/2025 through 27/08/2025. No login was required. YEAR 2024 page: a hub, not a listing - zero document links; it links to five per-crop leaf pages. On /web/fitosanitario/bollettini-viticoli the entire 2024 vite season is published as INLINE HTML on one 258,197-byte page: 21 bulletin headings with 21 in-page anchors (#Bollettino...), dates 04 aprile 2024 to 30 agosto 2024, and ZERO downloadable files. Same inline pattern on the other four crops (frutticoli 34 headings, olivicoli 44, orticoli 46, seminativi 1), all stamped "13 agosto 2026". So for VITE before 2026 the archive holds 20 PDFs (2025, on a second host) plus 21 HTML-only bulletins (2024). Nothing earlier was found on-site: guessed year paths 2023/2022/2021/2020 all return a clean 404 (identical 50,391-byte error page), the site search returned no pre-2024 bulletin page on result page 1, the declared sitemap.xml holds only one fitosanitario URL and it is an org-chart page, and a legacy mirror host elezioni2020.regione.veneto.it serves a byte-for-byte equivalent 2024 page with no older years. Absence here is NOT proof the pre-2024 bulletins never existed - only that this site does not currently link them. Downloaded 6 documents as proof of file type; verified all four PDF samples begin with %PDF-. Two robots.txt constraints found that a bulk pass must respect.

One suggestive trace: an anchor on the 2024 vite page targets '#Bollettino del 01 settembre 2023' while its visible label reads 04.04.2024, implying a 2023 edition once occupied that page. Not proof it is still retrievable anywhere.

measurements.name: PDF_TEXT_LAYER
measurements.evidence: No PDF library is installed locally (pypdf absent), so only a dependency-free probe was run. It inflated just 1-2 of 37-77 streams per file and extracted 0 text operators; 22-52 image XObjects per file were seen, and /Font markers appear in 2 of the 4 samples. This is a limitation of MY parser, not evidence that the PDFs lack a text layer. Do not read it as 'these are scans'.

measurements.name: AUTH_REQUIRED
measurements.evidence: No login, CAPTCHA or paywall was encountered on any of the 49 URLs probed. The sharing.regione.veneto.it Nextcloud shares serve their PDFs anonymously via /download.

blockers.detail: For User-agent: * the file sets crawl-delay: 10 and Disallow: /documents/ plus Disallow: /c/documents/. That is exactly the path holding all 106 of the 2026 PDFs (including the 20 vite bulletins). This is a crawl-policy constraint, not a technical block: the files themselves return 200 application/pdf. A bulk preservation pass must decide this explicitly rather than by accident, and honour the 10-second delay. I fetched 6 sample documents for type-proof before reading robots.txt and stopped there; no bulk fetching was performed.

The entire host is disallowed: 'User-agent: *' / 'Disallow: /' (26 bytes). This host carries all 20 of the 2025 vite PDFs and 9 crop guides linked from the Approfondimenti tecnici page. Again a policy constraint, not an access block - the /download URLs return 200 application/pdf anonymously.

The site search paginates through href='javascript:document.searchForm.action=...' controls, so only result page 1 (19 non-navigation links) could be read with curl. Deeper result pages were NOT retrieved. Any claim that pre-2024 bulletins are absent from the search index is therefore unproven.

All 11 documents on this page (2021 webinar decks, several on vine diseases such as Flavescenza dorata, giallumi and malattie del legno) are hosted on drive.google.com/file/d/<id>/view, outside regione.veneto.it. Their persistence is controlled by a third party and their availability was not tested.

not_known: Whether Veneto vite bulletins exist for any year before 2024, anywhere. Nothing pre-2024 was found on-site, but four search avenues each have a hole: guessed 404s only disprove the paths I guessed, site-search page 2+ is JavaScript-gated and was not read, sitemap.xml appears partial at 600 entries, and no external archive (Wayback and similar) was queried from this front.

Whether the sample PDFs carry a machine-readable text layer or are image-only scans. My dependency-free probe inflated only 1-2 of 37-77 streams per file and is not competent to answer this. NOT a finding of 'no text'.
The page count and the actual editorial content of the four downloaded PDFs. File type is proven (%PDF- magic, 0.86-4.26 MB); the contents were not read.
Whether the sharing.regione.veneto.it share tokens are permanent or expire. All 7 tested resolved today; no expiry metadata was inspected.
Why the 2025 vite bulletins moved to a separate Nextcloud host while 2026 returned to the portal, and whether the 2025 portal folder still exists behind an unlinked URL.
Whether the 2024 inline HTML bulletins were ever also published as PDFs. The five 2024 crop pages carry zero document links today; that is not proof no PDF was ever issued.

What the 'Bollettino colture erbacee' and 'Bollettino agrometeo' headings on the 2026 and 2025 year pages point at - both headings render with 0 document links beneath them in the served HTML. Whether they are empty sections, awaiting publication, or broken was not determined.
Whether elezioni2020.regione.veneto.it is a deliberate archival mirror or an incidental alias. It served byte-equivalent content for every path tested and exposed no additional years.

Total document counts for the non-vite comparti before 2024, and whether ARPAV's Servizio Agrometeo (linked from the archive index) holds a parallel and deeper bulletin series. Not probed from this front.
next_steps: Preserve the 2024 season as HTML, not as files. Snapshot the five crop pages (bollettini-viticoli 258197 b, -frutticoli 267363 b, -olivicoli 206414 b, -orticoli-industriali 178172 b, -seminativi 45616 b) and split each by its in-page anchors into 146 individual bulletin records (21 of them vite). These pages are the only copy - there is no PDF behind them, so a PDF-only harvester would silently record 2024 as empty.

Decide the robots question explicitly before any bulk pass. www.regione.veneto.it disallows /documents/ (all 106 2026 PDFs) and sharing.regione.veneto.it disallows everything (all 20 2025 vite PDFs). Either seek written permission from the U.O. Fitosanitario at fitosanitari@regione.veneto.it, or restrict automated collection to the HTML index and inline pages, which robots.txt does not disallow.

Harvest the 40 remaining vite PDFs from the manifests already written: 18 more from 2026 (raw/F1b-veneto-fito/year_2026_doclinks.json, crop=='vite') and 18 more from 2025 (raw/F1b-veneto-fito/vite_links_2025.json, appending /download to each share URL). Honour crawl-delay: 10. Expect roughly 0.9-4.3 MB per file, so on the order of 60-90 MB for the vite series alone.

Install a real PDF library (pypdf or pdfminer.six) in an isolated environment and settle PDF_TEXT_LAYER on the four files already on disk at raw/F1b-veneto-fito/. If they are image-only, every downstream plan that assumes text extraction needs OCR budgeted, and that changes the cost of the whole corpus.

Re-run the site search through a rendering browser to read result pages 2 and beyond for 'bollettino viticolo 2023' and 'bollettini fitosanitari'. Only that can turn today's 'nothing found before 2024' into either a real finding or a real absence.

Chase the 2023 trace concretely: the 2024 vite page contains an anchor targeting '#Bollettino del 01 settembre 2023' whose visible label reads 04.04.2024. Query an external web archive for https://www.regione.veneto.it/web/fitosanitario/bollettini-viticoli with captures dated 2023 and 2024 - the editing history suggests earlier seasons occupied that exact URL.

Ask the U.O. Fitosanitario directly whether pre-2024 bulletins are retrievable, and whether a bulk or machine-readable feed exists. Published contacts on the pages fetched: fitosanitari@regione.veneto.it and agroalimentare@regione.veneto.it. Do not send anything without the user's explicit approval of the message text.

Probe ARPAV's Servizio Agrometeo (https://www.arpa.veneto.it/dati-ambientali/bollettini/agrometeo/agrometeoinforma), linked from the archive index as the companion meteorological source, to see whether it holds a longer or independently archived series.

Record the two-host split in whatever schema stores this corpus: the same vite series lives on www.regione.veneto.it/documents/ for 2026, on sharing.regione.veneto.it for 2025, and as inline HTML for 2024. A single URL pattern will not fetch all three, and assuming one will is how a year goes missing.
